paragraphs.title: Taking Refuge in God and His Protection

answers: In the secret place of the most High
In the fortress of the enemy
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, "He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High."
easy.q: Where does the person dwell at the beginning of the psalm?

easy.explanation: The speaker says, "He is my refuge and my fortress."
easy.q: What does the person call the LORD?

answers: With His feathers and under His wings
easy.explanation: The verse says, "He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust."
easy.q: How does the LORD protect the person according to verse 4?

answers: A desire to leave the LORD
medium.explanation: The words "in him will I trust" clearly express confidence in God.
medium.q: What does the speaker express by saying, "in him will I trust"?

answers: From a fortress and from war
From the snare of the fowler and the noisome pestilence
medium.explanation: Verse 3 names "the snare of the fowler" and "the noisome pestilence."
medium.q: From what does the LORD deliver the person according to verse 3?

medium.explanation: A fowler catches birds with a snare, so the phrase refers to a trap.
medium.q: What does "the snare of the fowler" mean in context?

answers: Both describe a place of refuge
challenge.explanation: Both phrases picture safety and shelter found with God.
challenge.q: What connection exists between "the secret place of the most High" and "under the shadow of the Almighty"?

answers: It describes the size of the danger
It shows that God's faithfulness is a protection
It identifies the person's dwelling place
challenge.explanation: God's truth is described as "thy shield and buckler," showing that His faithfulness protects.
challenge.q: What does "his truth" contribute to the description of protection?

challenge.explanation: The passage moves from dwelling with God to trusting Him, receiving deliverance, and resting under His protection.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in verses 1–4?

paragraphs.title: Protection from Fear, Calamity, and the Wicked

answers: The terror by night and the arrow by day
easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, "Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day."
easy.q: What will the person not be afraid of according to verse 5?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, "A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand."
easy.q: What happens to the thousand and the ten thousand?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, "Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked."
easy.q: What does the person behold with his eyes?

medium.explanation: The verses mention terror by night, arrows by day, pestilence in darkness, and destruction at noonday.
medium.q: What dangers are mentioned in verses 5–6?

answers: The dangers are limited to certain hours
The person is protected at all times
medium.explanation: Because threats are described at different times, God's protection is shown to be continual.
medium.q: What does the contrast between night, day, darkness, and noonday teach?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes a destructive power that wastes or brings ruin in broad daylight.
medium.q: What does "the destruction that wasteth at noonday" describe?

answers: He cannot see what is happening
He receives special protection in the midst of danger
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts the falling of many with the statement, "but it shall not come nigh thee."
challenge.q: What is the significance of many falling around the person while the danger does not come near him?

answers: The dangers are described first, and the reward of the wicked is seen afterward
The dangers disappear because a fortress is built
Verse 8 introduces a new danger to the person
challenge.explanation: After describing many threats and destruction, the passage ends with the person seeing the reward of the wicked.
challenge.q: How do verses 5–6 connect with verse 8?

answers: Freedom from fear despite many threats
challenge.explanation: The passage repeatedly says that the protected person will not fear terror, arrows, pestilence, or destruction.
challenge.q: What quality of the person taking refuge in God is especially emphasized?

paragraphs.title: God as Refuge and His Angels as Guardians

easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, "Because thou hast made the LORD, which is my refuge."
easy.q: Who is the person's refuge according to verse 9?

easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, "For he shall give his angels charge over thee."
easy.q: Over whom does the LORD command the person to be guarded?

answers: They hide the person in a cave
They lead the person into battle
They bear the person up in their hands
easy.explanation: The verse says, "They shall bear thee up in their hands."
easy.q: What do the angels do according to verse 12?

answers: Dwelling with God is connected with protection from harm
The habitation causes the person to leave the refuge
The habitation is the dwelling place of the wicked
medium.explanation: The passage connects making the LORD a refuge and habitation with the promise that evil and plague will not come near.
medium.q: What is the connection between making the most High a habitation and evil not coming near?

answers: So he will not see the way
So he will not dash his foot against a stone
So he can reach the wicked
medium.explanation: Verse 12 gives the purpose: "lest thou dash thy foot against a stone."
medium.q: Why do the angels bear the person up in their hands?

medium.explanation: A habitation is a place where someone dwells; here it means making the Most High one's dwelling place.
medium.q: What does "habitation" mean in the phrase "the most High, thy habitation"?

answers: The passage moves from emphasizing refuge to emphasizing active guardianship
The passage moves from protection to the fall of the wicked
The passage moves from safety to fear at night
challenge.explanation: First the LORD is presented as refuge; then His angels are commanded to guard and carry the person.

answers: The protection extends to all his ways and prevents stumbling
The protection exists only inside the house
The person is not allowed to travel
challenge.explanation: The verses describe protection in all the person's ways and preservation from striking his foot.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the angels keeping the person "in all thy ways" and carrying him in their hands?

answers: As people who fall around him
challenge.explanation: The angels are charged to keep the person and bear him up in their hands.
challenge.q: How are the angels portrayed in relation to the person?

paragraphs.title: Complete Protection and the Promise of Salvation

easy.explanation: Verse 13 says, "Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder."
easy.q: Which creatures will the person tread upon?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, "He shall call upon me, and I will answer him."
easy.q: What does the LORD promise to do when the person calls upon Him?

easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, "With long life will I satisfy him."
easy.q: With what will the LORD satisfy the person?

answers: Be with the person, deliver him, and honor him
medium.explanation: The LORD says, "I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him."
medium.q: What does the LORD promise to do in trouble?

answers: Calling, answering, presence in trouble, deliverance, and honor
medium.explanation: Verse 15 gives this sequence: the person calls, God answers, remains with him in trouble, delivers him, and honors him.
medium.q: What sequence of actions appears in the LORD's answer to the person who calls?

answers: I will place him in a secure and exalted position
I will hide My name from him
medium.explanation: To set someone on high is to raise him to a protected and honored place.
medium.q: What does "I will set him on high" mean in context?

answers: Dangers and enemies that the person overcomes
challenge.explanation: These dangerous creatures are presented as things the protected person will tread upon or trample.
challenge.q: What do the lion, adder, young lion, and dragon represent in this passage?

answers: The speaker begins describing the wicked
The LORD Himself speaks and makes promises
challenge.explanation: These verses contain God's direct promises: "I will deliver him," "I will answer him," and "I will be with him."
challenge.q: What change occurs in the speaker's voice in verses 14–16?

answers: From presence in trouble to deliverance, honor, long life, and salvation
From protection to fear and defeat
From calling to silence and distance
challenge.explanation: The promise expands from God's presence in trouble to deliverance, honor, long life, and seeing His salvation.
challenge.q: How does the divine promise develop from the end of verse 15 into verse 16?
